deferrals.summary: Rename test.lock to heavy.lock and BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_* to BENCHBOX_HEAVY_* once the guard is stable

description:
## Problem
Nothing shows who holds the host lock, who waits, which VMs reserve memory, or which orphaned servers still run. Agents start servers by hand outside every entry point (two QuestDB JVMs orphaned to launchd, one at 2.3 GB RSS, cwd in BenchBox worktrees; no repo code launches them). Agents need the rule as early as possible in the rollout.

## Change
1. `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock status` and `make heavy-status`: holder record and age, live waiters, admission readings, VM inventory, top 10 processes by physical footprint, orphaned JVMs/servers (ppid 1, cwd inside a BenchBox worktree). Read-only; per-command 5 s timeouts.
2. `make heavy-run CMD="..."` wrapping `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run --guard -- sh -c "$(CMD)"`.
3. AGENTS.md `[HEAVY-LOCK-001]` (compact) linking `docs/agent/heavy-work.md`: heavy work runs only through entry points that take the lock or through `make heavy-run`; hand-started servers run under `make heavy-run` and are stopped afterwards; check `make heavy-status` first; never move, delete or recreate the lock file; never set `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force` or `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off` without owner approval in the current task. The detail doc also records known limits: fork-without-exec children inherit the flock; `kill -9` of a `run` wrapper leaves its child unlocked; VM memory is not tree-attributed.
4. `make/help.mk` lines for the new targets.
5. Record a deferral for the optional rename (`test.lock` -> `heavy.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_*` -> `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_*`).

## Decision gates
- G1: AGENTS.md rule stays within ~6 lines; detail goes to `docs/agent/heavy-work.md` (unpublished; not in docs/publish-allowlist.txt).
- G2: status never needs the lock and finishes within 5 s with a hung `container` CLI.
- G3: if heavy-guard-watchdog has landed, `heavy-run` uses `--guard` and this item smokes it with a tiny budget; if not, `heavy-run` uses lock+admission and heavy-guard-watchdog switches it.

## Guardrails (all heavy-guard items)
- Linked worktree from `origin/develop` via `make worktree-create`; never the primary clone; stage paths explicitly; never `git add -A`.
- `[COMMENT-POLICY-001]`: no comments or docstrings in new code. Durations use `benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()`/`elapsed_seconds()`.
- Tests use `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR` under `tmp_path` and injected readings; never touch the real `~/.benchbox/test.lock` or depend on live host pressure, VMs or disk.
- Never delete, move or recreate a lock file from code; never stop, resize or signal processes/VMs this invocation did not start.
- Keep names `test.lock`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS`, `BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK`, `BENCHBOX_TEST_SESSION_OWNER` (rename deferred on heavy-guard-status-policy).
- No automatic skip on `CI` or `BENCHBOX_EPHEMERAL_CLONE` (agent shells export `CI=true`).
- No heavy verification runs (no benchmark sweeps above scale 0.01, no real compose stacks) unless the item names one.
- Status never signals or modifies processes, VMs or the lock file.

## Non-goals
Killing orphans automatically (see heavy-guard-sentinel).
